evidence_items.locator: Results, analysis of 30 interaction transcripts; Methods, Participants
evidence_items.explanation: Complete-case performance exceeded lay-user performance, and 16 of 30 inspected interactions began with incomplete information. However, later information sometimes corrected omissions or introduced new errors; the experiment randomized access to a chatbot, not whether missing facts were elicited.

The published AMIE evaluation demonstrates useful history-taking by a specialized LLM system in simulated consultations. This is counterevidence to universal incapacity, but its patient-actors and research system differ from ordinary public chatbot use; the date identifies publication, not verified trial dates.

unresolved_gaps: No cited experiment isolates the causal effect of asking the missing questions in otherwise matched lay-user conversations.
